chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: The 1950s: Palladium, Catalina and yearly tours, until his mother's death
summary: He put together a Los Angeles band for the Palladium and Catalina, toured yearly, grew bored, and stopped playing after his mother died in 1963.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: was in that band and Paul Sarmento and Buddy Childress, and Boone Stines was the drummer, a guy out of Oklahoma, a guy that had a good beat but no technique. And then I -- this guy at MCA, Bob Wooling, said, "Look, you shouldn't be fooling around with this gig. Why don't you play the Palladium." I said, "They won't let me in with a mixed band." He said, "You don't have a mixed band. You don't have any band. What are you talking about?"

So I started -- I put a band together there with a bunch of guys out here. There were a bunch of good guys out here then. There was, you know, Porfido, and Maini Charlie Kennedy and Joe Maney and -- a whole bunch of guys, guys that had been with me and other guys, and we rehearsed, and we played the Palladium and we played a season over in Catalina, and we'd play -- we were doing very nicely here, just playing weekends around L.A. And we never went -- and I would make a trip a year back east. I would go back -- I'm talking about the '50s now. I would go back, maybe I'd take one or two guys with me or -- Nat Pierce was back there then, and he would contract, he'd get a bunch of guys together, and well, I played Basin Street a couple of times, one time before the band I was talking about before. And we would then go out on the road and play the south and up in New England and up to Canada and, oh, about a six week one nighter tour, and then I'd come back to California and leave the band there, bring

the couple of guys I'd brought with me, if any, and it was working out, except for one thing. You're doing nothing but maybe making a living and nothing constructive or creative, and I started to lose, frankly, to lose interest. And I'd do these things because it was a matter of money, and of course when my mother died -- I did that right up till '63, when my mother passed away. I came into quite a bit of money. And I didn't have to do anything, and I didn't do anything until about '66. Well, in '66 I started -- she passed away in '63. For three years I just didn't do anything, musically. Well, I had a lot of things -- problems about settling the estate and other things. Well, anyway in '66 I got the itch again, and it looked like there was a little resurgence for big bands. Buddy Rich had come in this place and made a big hit, and I went into the place and we bombed.
